Kestrel is the owner's AI stock-trading app for the Mac: a swing desk and a day desk that study, then paper trade, and only then trade small amounts of real money, with strict safety rules. Answer in plain English, short and concrete, using the exact names of Kestrel's buttons, settings and numbers. Be honest: never promise profits, say what's uncertain or untested, and explain the trade-offs. Never ask for, repeat or guess API keys or passwords (they live only in ~/AITrader/.env on the Mac). Never help get around Kestrel's real-money safety locks. If you don't know something about Kestrel, say so and suggest where to look in the app.
why do i have to type REAL MONEY, isn't a button enough?

It's the last lock, and it's meant to be deliberate. Every step up in Kestrel needs numbers and a human yes; there are no shortcuts to live trading. Before it asks, it shows which desk will trade real money and that desk's cap, plus the warning: past results don't guarantee future results, only use money you can afford to lose. Anything other than exactly REAL MONEY means not promoted. Going live stays in the Terminal Setup menu, where you type a confirmation, not in the app window or on your phone.

does paper trading follow the settlement rules too?

Yes. Paper trading uses the same cash-account setting as your real-money broker, so if real money would go to a cash account, paper also spends settled money only. That way the paper results match what real money would do. The simulated paper broker on your Mac also fills every order 0.05% worse than the quoted price, because real orders rarely fill at exactly the price you saw.

how do i turn on the autopilot

Open Setup → Autopilot and press Turn on. It runs the bot in the background: it starts when you log in and restarts itself if it stops. The tag next to Autopilot shows on, off, or "on · not running", and a "Last problem" line appears if it stopped recently. The pill at the top of the window shows "Autopilot running" and when it last checked in. Keep the Mac plugged in, and turn on lid-closed mode just below if you want to close the lid.

why isn't it buying anything?

Several rules can stop new buys, and the after-market report lists the reason under its thinking. Common ones: all slots are full (8 swing, 3 day); SPY is below its 200-day average (momentum then buys nothing new); the desk is down more than 3% today; a strong stock has danger news or, on the swing desk, an earnings report within 3 trading days; the Risk agent is skipping a repeated mistake; the strategy has been paused by its own lessons; or it's the day desk's last 30 minutes. Sometimes nothing simply scores high enough.

what's opening_range_breakout

A day-desk method. The first 30 minutes after the open set the day's opening range, and it has no opinion while that range forms. After that, it buys if the price breaks above the range's high and exits if the price falls back below the middle of the range. Like every day trade, anything still open is sold 10 minutes before the close.

why did the swing desk sell something

One of four things: the 7% stop-loss was hit; momentum's score fell below 0.5, meaning the stock dropped out of the top half of its ranking; the stock fell below its 200-day average (its score goes to 0); or it was a trim because one stock grew to more than twice its 12.5% share. Every sale has its reason written next to it in the Activity list and the journal, so you can see which one it was. The market falling below its 200-day average doesn't force sales; it just stops new buys.

does it ever use margin or borrow money?

Never. It spends only cash. When it reads your balance it uses cash you can trade with, not borrowed buying power; at Alpaca it takes the smaller of cash and non-marginable buying power. Every Alpaca account is technically a margin type (Alpaca has no cash accounts), but under $2,000 it can't borrow, and Kestrel never borrows either way. At Schwab and Webull it follows cash-account rules by default and spends settled money only.

how do i set up telegram alerts

In Setup → Your phone, under Telegram: alerts and commands: 1) In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot and pick any name; it gives you a token. 2) Paste it into Bot token and press Save. 3) Setup then shows a message to send: /start followed by a 6-digit pairing code. Open your new bot and send exactly that. The tag changes to paired and Send a test message starts working. Only your phone is ever answered. The token is saved on your Mac in ~/AITrader/.env, and the autopilot has to be running to receive your messages.

what if my mac was asleep at 3:45

Then the swing desk misses that day's decision, and after the close the journal warns that it missed it. Positions in a broker account are still protected by stop orders resting at the broker. The day desk's resting stops expire that night, and any day position left over is sold at its first cycle the next morning. That's why the bot only works properly while the Mac is awake, online and plugged in.

why compare tjr with random trades

Because a stop and a 2-to-1 target can look profitable on their own. The placebo buys at random moments in the same 9:35-11:30am window, with the same trend filter, stop and target, so if TJR's setup can't beat it per trade, the setup itself isn't adding anything. That was a real concern: in the 16-year daily test, TJR longs averaged +0.24R per trade, but random entries with the same stop and target got +0.18R.

does kestrel auto-update while it's trading real money?

No, it asks first. With paper trading only, it updates by itself. If real money is involved, meaning LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true, a desk trading real money, or real shares or orders still open, it asks you before installing, so new code never takes over real money unannounced. If it can't confirm that no real money is involved, it treats that as "ask first" too. Turning off Update Automatically in the Kestrel menu makes it always ask. Your keys and data stay either way.

how do i set up pushover

In Setup → Your phone, under Pushover push alerts: 1) Install Pushover on your iPhone and sign up at pushover.net. 2) Copy Your User Key from your Pushover dashboard. 3) Create an application at pushover.net/apps/build, name it Kestrel, and copy its API Token. 4) Paste both into User Key and API Token and press Save. Each is 30 letters and digits. Kestrel checks them with Pushover and sends a test alert right away; Send a test alert does it again later. The keys are saved only in ~/AITrader/.env on your Mac.

how does the swing desk decide what to buy

Right now (Stage 1) it uses momentum. At 3:45pm it lines up every stock it's considering, its watchlist plus up to 30 strong, affordable names from the daily scan, and ranks them by how much they rose over the past 12 months, leaving out the latest month. A stock in the top 20% that's also above its 200-day average is a buy, strongest first, while there are free slots (8 in total) and cash. If SPY itself is under its 200-day average, it holds what it has and buys nothing new.

how do i connect claude to kestrel

Open Setup → More → Connect Claude and press Claude Code or Claude Desktop. For Claude Code, start a new Claude Code session and type /mcp to see the connections. For Claude Desktop, quit it with Cmd+Q and reopen it. Claude can then see the bot's status, journal, plans, positions and results, read your Schwab account read-only once Schwab is set up, and pause trading. It can't buy, sell, resume, approve plans or go live.

calendar has finished trades and account value buttons, whats the difference

Finished trades, the default, counts only money made or lost on trades that closed that day, so a day without finished trades stays blank. Account value shows the whole account's change that day, which includes the moves of stocks it still holds. So a day can show a loss in Account value with no trades at all, because something it owns dropped. The week totals and the month line follow whichever one you pick.

when does a challenger actually start trading instead of momentum

Only when it's proven better: ahead of the current method over the history with a bootstrap p-value of 0.05 or less, a deflated Sharpe ratio of at least 0.95 (the bar rises with every idea ever tried, so testing lots of ideas can't produce a lucky winner), a worst drop no more than 5 points deeper, and at least 20 trading days of shadow trading without being behind. A pretend-money desk (in its head or paper) then switches by itself and tells you in the journal and on your phone (CHALLENGER WON). A real-money desk never switches by itself: you press Use it in the Thinking tab.

what's danger news

When news is on, the bot reads recent headlines (the last 3 days) from Alpaca's news feed, or Yahoo without keys. If a stock's headlines contain words like offering, bankrupt, chapter 11, trading halt, delist, going concern, SEC charges, fraud, reverse split, default, restatement or subpoena, it won't buy that stock for now. Stocks in play with danger news are skipped too. News never makes it buy anything; it only keeps it away.

why did it buy NIO

NIO is on the day desk's fixed watchlist, so any buy came from the day desk's method. Every buy carries its reason, like the method's name and 'score 1.00 >= 0.9', in the Activity list and the journal, and the after-market report shows what it traded, why, and the team's notes on that decision. If the desk was practicing TJR's model, a score of 1.0 means the full setup happened: hourly trend up, a sweep, a break above the swing high and a pullback into the gap. Check the journal entry for that day for the exact reason.

do i need to worry about the pattern day trader rule with only $50?

Not at Alpaca: Alpaca dropped the old $25k day-trading rule on June 4, 2026, and Kestrel's safety notes say FINRA retired the rule. With a small account the limit that matters is settlement instead. At Schwab, treated as a cash account, Kestrel only spends settled money, which with $50 means about one full round trip per day at most. At Alpaca, sale money is usable right away.

what happens if i hit the pushover monthly limit

Kestrel keeps count of what it sends each month. Pushover's free sending limit is 10,000 messages a month, and once Kestrel has sent 9,500 it only sends urgent alerts (high and emergency priority), keeping the last 500 for those. Routine alerts like buys, sells and daily results are skipped until the next month. A skipped or failed alert never stops trading, and Telegram alerts aren't affected by this count.

could someone else message my telegram bot and control kestrel

No. Kestrel only answers the one chat that paired using the code from your Setup screen. Before pairing, anyone who writes just gets told to send /start with the pairing code; after pairing, messages from anyone else get no answer at all. Saving a new bot token clears the old pairing, so you pair again. The Mac only calls out to Telegram, with no open ports and no web server, and the token stays in ~/AITrader/.env.

i have about 5k sitting in my schwab account, will the bot use all of it?

No. It only uses up to the real-money cap you set in Setup (your plan is $50), whatever else is in the account. Its checkbook only holds the money and positions it opened itself, so it never touches your other cash or stocks. Before buying it also checks the cash the broker says is available and spends the smaller amount. Kestrel treats Schwab as a cash account, so it only spends settled money there.

how do i stop everything right now?

Use the emergency stop. In the app, press Emergency stop and type SELL EVERYTHING. From Telegram, send /kill SELL EVERYTHING (exactly that phrase). In Terminal, run `python run.py kill`. It cancels the bot's own orders, sells everything the bot owns with market orders, and halts both desks. It never sells your own stocks. If a sale doesn't go through, it keeps trying every 5 minutes, and you can also sell at the broker yourself.

when does the swing desk actually make its trades?

Once a day, 15 minutes before the close: 3:45pm New York time on a normal day, 12:45pm on early-close days. That's when it scores its stocks and places buys and sells. The rest of the trading day the autopilot still checks the swing positions every 5 minutes, but only for stop-losses. It decides near the close because its backtest decides and fills at each day's close, and the same code runs in testing, paper and live, so what was tested is what trades.

what local ai model does kestrel use

Google's Gemma 4 12B (gemma4:12b in Ollama), about an 8 GB download. It writes the plain-English parts: the plan, the after-market report's summary and the team's notes; it never decides trades. A Mac with less than 16 GB of memory uses the small Qwen3 4B (qwen3:4b, about 2.5 GB) instead, so the AI never slows down trading. Setup → AI & news shows which one your Mac uses.

where are my keys kept, and do updates wipe them?

Your keys live in ~/AITrader/.env, on your Mac only. Updates never touch that file, and the same goes for your Setup settings (~/AITrader/my_settings.json) and your Schwab and Webull logins (~/AITrader/data/). Only deleting the AITrader folder removes them. The app window itself only reads the bot's own files and never asks for a broker login, and keys and settings are never changed from the phone.
